A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VRL research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material against v2's added appendix evaluations.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on iNaturalist and Kiki-Bouba, feature-fusion experiments, and classifier/model ablations in the main text and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original mini-ImageNet results, scalability evaluations, and human assessment of generated features in Appendices B.3–B.5.

M1.justification: The paired inter-class/intra-class feature extraction, VLM feature mapping, and downstream classifiers remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A.1. The added scaling experiments use existing CLIP mapping and pair sampling, without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained iNaturalist species and Kiki-Bouba recognition tasks, v2 adds general few-shot classification on mini-ImageNet and family-level classification spanning 200 iNaturalist families and 1,000 species. These substantially broaden the represented data and classification tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated LaBo-7B and LaBo-70B comparators. New Table 11 compares VRL with published results from F. Liu, M. Liu, and Chen on mini-ImageNet, substantially extending the comparison methods. Table 2's Kiki-Bouba comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include 5-way 1-shot episodic evaluation, training-data scaling through 10/50/200 images per class, specified pair-sampling budgets, and human scoring of 100 features for faithfulness and relevance. These are added experimental designs; the original main-table settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendices B.4–B.5 add training-data scaling against supervised fine-tuning, a larger family-classification scalability test, and a direct human audit of feature quality with an accuracy-correlation analysis. These extend the retained fusion, classifier, feature-mapping, and model-size ablations.

E5.justification: Where the original result tables report point estimates, Table 11 adds explicit numerical uncertainty, including VRL's 94.27 ± 0.05, and Appendix B.3 specifies 1,000 testing episodes. The meaning of ± is undefined, and no increase in independent runs or seeds is established.

E6.justification: Existing accuracy entries in Tables 1–5 and 9–10 are unchanged. Added results include LaBo averages of 43.00/51.72, mini-ImageNet accuracy of 94.27 ± 0.05, VRL/SFT accuracies of 86.2/80.2 at 200 images per class, and family-classification accuracies of 73/83/90 for CLIP/VRL/combined features. The human study reports 93% faithful/relevant features and a 0.84 correlation with accuracy.

T1.justification: The pairing definitions and Appendix A.2 complexity arguments are retained. The added expression F = VLM(y, x) merely restates the existing feature-mapping operation; no new theorem, proof, assumption, or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: interpretable verbalized features, few-shot generalization, and improved classification with less data. The headline 24% and 20% absolute-gain claims are retained; the added evaluations provide supporting evidence rather than redefine those claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for soft voting's robustness, attributes scaling performance to verbalized-query priors, and discusses combining coarse VLM distinctions with finer task-specific features. Appendix B.5 also argues that lower classifier weights reduce the influence of irrelevant or hallucinated features.

D1.justification: v2 identifies use of LaBo's official implementation and clarifies the source of human-labeled attributes. Appendix A.2 removes the separate ten-minute feature-mapping timing and adds single-A6000 extraction information plus an LLM-Mutate runtime comparison. Prompt templates, classifier hyperparameters, and access to the same code repository remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 expands citations to language/concept bottlenecks, recent few-shot comparators, CLIP-Event, and SOLO, while removing the interpretable-basis-decomposition reference. It refines the discussion of LaBo and LLM-Mutate but retains the central positioning of visually grounded features against attributes derived from pretrained knowledge.

P1.justification: The introduction and baseline discussion receive localized rewrites, terminology and grammar corrections, and expanded explanations. v2 adds an author/affiliation, acknowledgements, and Appendices B.3–B.5, while preserving the overall narrative and section organization.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 11–13 and two LaBo rows to Table 1. Figure 1 changes the illustrative icons and refines its caption. Existing figures and tables otherwise retain their organization, with limited resizing and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The added LaBo comparison, broader recognition evaluations, scalability tests, and direct human feature audit strengthen evidence beyond v1's selected recognition tasks and qualitative examples. The gain is limited by sparse reporting of the new protocols, undefined uncertainty notation, and missing human-rater details. Appendix A.2 also loses the separate feature-mapping timing, reducing clarity about computational cost.
